question: What is the California Ocean Observing System?
answer: Ocean observations provide information to track the onset and impacts of El Nino. Ocean observations provide real-time, on-the-ground information that allows climate scientists to assess El Nino intensity, geographic extent, and implications for society. In California, the Central & Northern California Ocean Observing System (CeNCOOS) and Southern Coastal California Ocean Observing System (SCCOOS) support a distributed network of observing stations and information tools to provide actionable information to inform decision-making. CeNCOOS and SCCOOS (also known as CalOOS) works closely with partner monitoring programs across the state including at Scripps, CalCOFI, MBARI, SWFSC, THL, ACESS, CDIP, NDBC, and many others.
